steps.do: Create DebouncedField.swift in the app target folder.
Store the pending work in a @State Task? property, and cancel it inside .onChange of the bound text on every change.
Inside the new Task, call Task.sleep with nanoseconds set to 200_000_000, then check Task.isCancelled before running the validation.
Write a unit test that makes three changes within 50ms and asserts that the validation ran exactly once.
Run the debounce test class on the simulator.

K-023773.example: Typing a, b, and c within 50ms cancels two pending tasks, so only the last task runs the check after 200ms. The test output should show DebounceTests passed with a validation count of 1.
K-023773.check: xcodebuild prints Test Suite 'DebounceTests' passed and ends with ** TEST SUCCEEDED **.
traps: Small models often forget to cancel the previous Task, so every keystroke still runs validation; always cancel before starting a new one.
Task.sleep(nanoseconds:) counts nanoseconds, so passing 200 sleeps only 200ns; use 200_000_000 for 200ms.
Do not run slow checks on the main actor; do the work in a Task and assign results back on MainActor.

traps: Small models set max-w-prose on a container that holds headings and buttons, which narrows the wrong elements.

traps: Small models use h-11 or w-11 instead of min-h-11 and min-w-11, which fixes the size exactly and can clip longer labels.
Icon-only buttons still need the minimum, so skip them and the test will fail.
Padding alone does not guarantee 44px, because the element can stay shorter than its content box.

traps: Small models check only the body text and skip the helper text, placeholders, and disabled states, which also need 4.5:1.
